I now have the privilege of delivering the State of the Town Address, reflecting on key 2020 accomplishments and 2021 priorities, including the vision we have set in motion for our future. So I will. And first and foremost, I'm happy to report that the State of our Town remains strong, and our future prospects are very bright, in spite of the uncertainty brought on by the pandemic. Our strength lies in the dedication of our Town employees, the enduring commitment and volunteerism of our residents, and the resiliency of our businesses, all reflected in how we responded to the pandemic. And I think it's worth mentioning some of the few exemplary highlights. We launched the We Love Local campaign, it seems like years ago, days after the shutdown was announced back in March, and we raised $300,000 for local businesses. We immediately pivoted to virtual operations across all departments. We offered a wide range of virtual classes and programming through our Recreation Department, who then successfully also opened Memorial Pool for a safe summer season. We created virtual Downtown Westfield as non-essential businesses were forced to close. We then welcomed Open Quimby with special events and festive outdoor dining spaces. We recreated popular community events, such as Alt Adams Fest and Drive Thru Santa. We created a virtual tree lighting that kicked off a food drive for the Community Food Bank, raising $50,000. We established the first virtual Zoom Court in Union County. We redirected the Police Department school resource officers to serve as community resource officers to assist seniors and residents in need. We created an online Coronavirus Information Center and held Facebook Live updates to address our community's pandemic questions. We delivered more than 125 written COVID updates to ensure residents had latest information and ready access to resources, which we continue to do. We contacted seniors via weekly wellness calls, and there was so much more, too long to list tonight. And while the pandemic consumed much of our focus, it did not deter us from making progress on the transformational plans for our Downtown and positioning Westfield for post-pandemic success. By recently designating StreetWorks Development as the developer for their Lord and Taylor properties in the train station parking lot, we culminated a public planning process that began almost three years ago to establish an overdue long-term vision for Westfield. Their designation marks the beginning of a new public and actionable phase in our planning, which will be a main focus of ours this year. In addition to these critical planning and redevelopment efforts, we also ensured throughout 2020 that we continued to deliver on the four key priorities I committed to when I was elected, strong fiscal oversight, charting a vision for our future, championing quality of life issues, and increasing resident engagement. While uncertainty over the fiscal impact of the pandemic deferred some key 2020 initiatives, I am proud of the accomplishments we made on many fronts this year. And I think it's important to reiterate some of the highlights. First and most importantly, we led our community through a global pandemic, which we are still doing, prioritizing health, safety, and communication, while also adapting operations to ensure the safety and welfare of employees, residents, and businesses. We reduced the town budget by over 1.3% in anticipation of pandemic-related revenue declines. It was the first decrease in eight years in spite of a 2% increase in non-discretionary expenses. We maintained a healthy $7 million budget surplus and AAA bond rating. We made significant progress on our downtown redevelopment plan, which was a giant leap towards our downtown transformation. We continued to prioritize our Raritan Valley fight for better service and peak one-seat rides by lobbying the governor, legislator, and New Jersey Transit as co-chair of the RVL Mayors Alliance, which I tried to get in with Senator Kaine tonight. We introduced park improvements at Mendewasken, Tamaquis, and Sycamore, and made significant progress on the Edison School Athletic Complex proposal in collaboration with the Board of Ed. We planted approximately 500 trees. We implemented new outdoor dining and land use policies that enabled improvements to downtown businesses, and received $833,000 in pursued grants, which I think was only second to last year in the first we had gotten, for most we've gotten in decades. We commemorated Westfield's 300th anniversary with a variety of events, not quite what we had planned, funded all by private donors and sponsors, including lectures, art displays, time capsule architectural tours, and the first African-American walking tour, and so much more. It was quite remarkable how much we were able to do in spite of the fact we're in the middle of a pandemic. We established a public arts commission, resulted in two new murals funded through grants and donations, and successful first public art installation, Art Takes Flight, our butterfly exhibit, which raised $24,000 through public art auction to fund future art exhibits. And very importantly, we awarded a silver certification by Sustainable Jersey, a first time we've ever been certified in town history, and increased eligibility for grants and funding. There is a much more exhaustive list of accomplishments that can be found on the town website, but I do wanna spend a bit of my time this evening focusing on our future. Our top priority in 2021, without question, is to continue to ensure the health and welfare of our employees, residents, and businesses. As the vaccine rolls out more broadly over the course of this year, we will begin to gradually reclaim normalcy. My position remains that we, as a forward-looking community, need to be ready to capitalize on our post-pandemic future through the groundwork we have laid over the last few years. In my State of the Town address last year, I talked about change, and what that means for us as a community. I mentioned that change is both hard and inevitable, but it's how we decide to address it that will define us. Who could have guessed how prescient those comments would prove to be, and the magnitude of the change that would be thrust upon us just a few months later? Remote work, remote school, Zoom meetings, social distancing, masking up, business shutdowns, stay-at-home orders, curbside pickup, online ordering, online everything. I believe wholeheartedly that how we respond to these sudden changes absolutely defined our community. If we weren't sure who we were then, we certainly do now. Resilient, compassionate, innovative, resourceful, adaptive, selfless. Many experts believe that COVID accelerated innovation in a number of areas by 10 years, which we have all personally experienced in some way. We now have the opportunity to harness this collective spirit of innovation towards working toward re-imagining a new future for our downtown, one that reflects the lifestyle and business landscape changes brought on by COVID in collaboration with StreetWorks with the following key objectives in mind. Expand and diversify our tax base in order to provide the amenities and services we deserve. Upgrade our aging infrastructure as we saw by water main break over the Christmas holidays and reduce our over-reliance on residential property taxes. Create opportunities to increase downtown daily and evening foot traffic by expanding downtown residential living and commercial office space, providing the walking wallets that will enable our businesses to thrive. Build on the success of Open Quimby by creating additional open spaces and public gathering spots. Diversify our housing stock by providing housing opportunities for newcomers and downsizers. Identify flexible post-COVID parking solutions for commuters, downtown residents, employees, and shoppers. Integrate arts and culture into the fabric of our downtown. Create and implement a streetscape improvement plan which includes sidewalks, lighting, signage, and landscaping. And very importantly, ensure the Lord and Taylor site is integrated as a critical component into our overall downtown plan. We are incredibly fortunate to have this significant opportunity right in front of us and it's ours to seize. While the retail environment is permanently altered and with competition from other towns and the lasting change brought about by this pandemic, I truly believe we cannot afford to do nothing. In addition to the potentially transformational opportunity our work will also focus on the following priorities. Implement a short-term post-pandemic downtown economic recovery plan beginning April 1st which will include to enhance Open Quimby aesthetically and with expanded programming to draw downtown visitors. Memorialize expanded outdoor dining. We've all seen the benefit and how much we've enjoyed it, quote, pandemic or not. Invest in beautifying the parklets and outdoor spaces and continue the Downtown Westville Corporation support of the online shopping portal Beyond Maine so our businesses have a chance to have a significant online presence as well. Secondly, we wanna continue to prioritize resident safety and security. Continue to focus and expand on community policing under the leadership of our police chief, Chris Battalora who's done such an exceptional job today who's also working to attain police accreditation for the first time in town history on our way to becoming a preeminent police department in the state thanks to his leadership. Third, we're gonna further the town hall culture of innovation and service. We've had several critical new hires in the last six months and we wanna empower these new hires and leadership roles with greater decision-making authority and what I call a get to yes mindset. We're launching a new user-friendly website as well as enhanced information technology capabilities which you'll see by second quarter. Fourthly, we wanna expand our parks and recreation opportunities and a big component of that and big priority is to finalize the Edison School athletic complex proposal in collaboration with the Board of Ed and anticipated public input. We wanna continue the progress we've made on Brightwood Park enhancements in collaboration with Friends of Brightwood. We wanna improve maintenance in Tamaquas Park to include bathrooms, cabins, water fountains and trails as well as a new rain garden that's currently underway. We wanna expand the sensory garden and landscaping at Mendewashten Park and we're gonna reprioritize proactive park maintenance with the DPW and we're gonna assess the staffing levels accordingly to make sure we can do so. And lastly, and fifth priority is the quality of life issues that matter to us all. And a big new initiative by Chairwoman Hapgood on the Finance Committee is to initiate a long range capital planning effort to increase investment in infrastructure and accelerate improvement in sewers, roads and drainage, always prioritizing sustainability and making green choices wherever possible. Once again, I'm gonna continue to fight for better service and peak one seat ride on the Verita Valley line and I think this pandemic has brought greater opportunity to do that. We'll finalize the circulation and traffic management recommendations by March which will inform future development. And we will aspire to attain sustainable Jersey gold certification building upon the green team's first ever certification where they achieved silver. So it's a long list but one I think we're very motivated to do. And so in closing, I look forward to the days when we return to in-person council meetings and the normalcy that they signify. As challenging as 2020 was for all of us, I hope we carry the positive lessons of the pandemic with us once that normalcy returns which includes prioritizing family, community, service and health. I will continue to ask that you commit yourself to remaining engaged and informed and to proactively stay on top of the information we share. Your input will be critical as we work together towards re-imagining the future of our downtown. I also ask that you continue holding us accountable for delivering on our commitment. And once again, approach this year with an open mind and a heart full of gratitude for being fortunate enough to live in this great community. This incredible town of Westfield has been in existence long before any of us and it will be here long after we're gone. Our task of this council is simply to leave it better than how we found it. It remains a privilege to be our mayor. God bless our great community and our incredible country. Happy new year, everyone. And I know we cannot wait to get to work. Thank you. And now I think it's time for open discussion by citizens. Please virtually raise your hand to make your comment on any subject on which we have jurisdiction and be sure to state your name and address for the record.
